title: 📘 UNIT 4: SOCIETY AND POLITICS IN THE AGE OF WORLD WARS 1914–1945
4.1 ⚔️ THE FIRST WORLD WAR: CAUSES, COURSE AND CONSEQUENCES
notes:
📅 First World War → 1914–1918.

🌍 It began mainly as a European conflict but involved countries from many regions, including Russia, the United States, the Middle East, and other parts of the world.

🧠 Major long-term causes → alliance rivalry, imperialism, militarism, nationalism, competition for colonies and growing mistrust among European powers.

🔥 Immediate cause → assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary by Serbian nationalist Gavrilo Princip at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914.

title: 4.1.1 🤝 MILITARY ALLIANCES BEFORE WWI
notes:
🛡️ Triple Alliance → Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy, formed in 1882. Italy later joined the opposing side in 1915.

🛡️ Triple Entente → developed from the Franco-Russian Alliance, the Anglo-French Entente Cordiale and the Anglo-Russian Agreement. Its leading members were Britain, France and Russia.

📌 Importance → the alliance system divided Europe into rival military camps and transformed a regional conflict into a wider European war.

title: 4.1.2 🌍 IMPERIALISM, MILITARISM AND NATIONALISM
notes:
🌍 Imperialism → European powers competed for colonies and economic influence in Africa and Asia, increasing rivalry and mistrust.

⚔️ Militarism → European states expanded armies and navies and gave the military greater influence in government policy.

🇫🇷🇩🇪 Nationalism → France wanted to regain Alsace and Lorraine after its defeat by Germany, while nationalist movements in the Balkans challenged Ottoman rule.

📌 These forces created an atmosphere in which a local crisis could develop into a major international war.

title: 4.1.3 🪖 COURSE OF WORLD WAR I
notes:
📅 28 July 1914 → Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia after Serbia rejected some demands of its ultimatum.

🇩🇪 Schlieffen Plan → Germany planned to defeat France quickly through Belgium before turning against Russia.

⚔️ Battle of the Marne → September 1914; stopped the German advance toward Paris.

⛏️ Western Front → both sides established defensive trenches, creating a long and deadly stalemate.

🇷🇺 Eastern Front → fighting was more mobile because Russia had greater territory and Germany had to fight on two fronts.

🇺🇸 United States → entered the war on 6 April 1917 after German unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram increased American hostility toward Germany.

title: 4.1.4 💥 CONSEQUENCES OF WORLD WAR I
notes:
💀 Human losses → millions of soldiers and civilians died, while many others were wounded or displaced.

⚔️ New warfare → machine guns, aircraft, poison gas and submarines increased the destructive power of war.

👑 Imperial collapse → the Habsburg, Hohenzollern, Ottoman and Romanov dynasties collapsed.

🦠 Spanish Flu → movement of soldiers and refugees helped spread the deadly influenza pandemic of 1918–1919.

🇷🇺 Russian Revolution → wartime hardship contributed to the fall of the Russian Empire and the rise of a socialist government.

📜 Treaty of Versailles → signed in 1919 and imposed severe penalties on Germany, including reparations, military restrictions and territorial losses.

🌍 Global impact → independence movements strengthened in colonies, while the United States became an increasingly important world power.

title: 4.2 🇷🇺 THE OCTOBER 1917 RUSSIAN REVOLUTION
notes:
🇷🇺 Russian Revolution → resulted from long-term opposition to Tsarist autocracy, economic backwardness, land problems, food shortages, social inequality and the destructive effects of World War I.

👥 Political groups → liberals wanted constitutional government, Social Revolutionaries emphasized peasant land reform, while Marxists sought revolutionary change.

☭ RSDLP → Russian Social Democratic Labour Party was formed in 1898 and later divided into Bolsheviks and Mensheviks.

👤 Bolsheviks → led by Vladimir Lenin and supported a more radical revolutionary program.

title: 4.2.1 🔥 FEBRUARY REVOLUTION
notes:
📅 February 1917 → strikes, demonstrations, food shortages and military discontent brought revolution to Petrograd.

👑 Result → Tsar Nicholas II was forced to abdicate, ending Romanov rule.

🏛️ Provisional Government → established by members of the Duma and first led by George Lvov, followed by Alexander Kerensky.

⚠️ Problem → the government failed to solve food shortages, land demands and the continuation of the war.

👥 Soviets → councils of workers, soldiers and peasants became powerful political bodies.

📌 February to October → Russia experienced a period of dual power between the Provisional Government and the Petrograd Soviet.

title: 4.2.2 ☭ OCTOBER REVOLUTION AND BOLSHEVIK RULE
notes:
📅 25 October 1917 → Bolsheviks led an armed uprising in Petrograd and seized the main government institutions.

👤 Leaders → Vladimir Lenin led the revolutionary government, with Leon Trotsky playing an important military role.

📢 Popular slogans → “Peace, Land and Bread” and “All Power to the Soviets!”

🏭 Economic measures → workers gained control of factories, industries were nationalized and an eight-hour working day was introduced.

🌾 Land reform → landlords’ estates were confiscated and land was given to peasants.

🕊️ Peace → Russia withdrew from World War I after signing the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany in 1918.

title: 4.2.3 🟥 CIVIL WAR, NEP AND THE USSR
notes:
⚔️ Russian Civil War → Red forces supporting the revolutionary government fought White forces made up mainly of anti-Bolshevik groups. The Red Army defeated the Whites by 1922.

💰 New Economic Policy, NEP → introduced in 1921. Small enterprises returned to private owners, peasants could sell grain for profit and commerce was revived.

🇷🇺 USSR → Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established in 1922.

👤 Lenin → died in 1924 and Joseph Stalin eventually became the dominant leader.

🏭 Five-Year Plans → Stalin promoted rapid industrialization and collectivization of agriculture.

🌍 Significance → the revolution inspired anti-colonial movements in Africa and Asia and strengthened socialism as a major global political force.

title: 4.3 🌐 LEAGUE OF NATIONS
notes:
📅 10 January 1920 → League of Nations formally established after World War I.

📍 Headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland.

🎯 Main aims → maintain international peace, promote collective security, encourage disarmament and settle disputes through negotiation and arbitration.

👤 Woodrow Wilson → strongly promoted the idea, but the United States never joined because the US Congress opposed commitments that could involve the country in European conflicts.

🏛️ Main organs → General Assembly, Secretariat and Executive Council.

title: 4.3.1 ⚠️ SUCCESS AND FAILURE OF THE LEAGUE
notes:
✅ Successes → the League helped settle some international disputes peacefully, including the Mosul dispute between Iraq and Turkey and a border dispute between Colombia and Peru.

❌ Weaknesses → the United States was absent, enforcement powers were limited and major powers were often unwilling to take strong action.

⚠️ Major failures → the League failed to stop Japanese aggression in China, Italian aggression against Ethiopia and other conflicts during the 1930s.

📌 Final result → the League could not prevent World War II and remained ineffective against aggressive totalitarian states. It continued to exist until 1946.

title: 4.4 📉 THE GREAT DEPRESSION
notes:
📅 Beginning → the Great Depression began with the Wall Street stock market crash in October 1929.

💰 Nature → it became the most severe economic crisis experienced by the industrialized world at that time.

📉 Effects → personal income, profits, tax revenue and prices declined, while international trade fell dramatically.

👷 Unemployment → reached extremely high levels, especially in the United States.

🏭 Industry → industrial production and construction declined sharply, causing businesses to close and workers to lose jobs.

🌾 Agriculture → falling crop prices severely affected farmers and rural communities.

📅 1933 → the crisis reached its lowest point in the United States, with millions unemployed and many banks having failed.

title: 4.5 🇮🇹 FASCISM IN ITALY
notes:
🧠 Fascism → authoritarian political ideology emphasizing dictatorship, extreme nationalism, one-party rule, militarism and strong state control.

👤 Benito Mussolini → formed the Fascist Party in 1919 and established a Fascist government in Italy in 1922.

📌 Causes of Fascism → disappointment with the postwar peace settlement, unemployment, economic crisis, social unrest, fear of communism and dissatisfaction with democratic government.

🎯 Mussolini → promised to restore Italian strength and national greatness.

title: 4.5.1 🏛️ IMPACT OF FASCISM IN ITALY
notes:
🏛️ Totalitarian rule → Mussolini weakened Parliament, dissolved opposition parties and established one-party control.

🚫 Political repression → opponents were terrorized, imprisoned or forced to flee.

👥 Social control → strikes and lockouts were prohibited and the state gained control over many areas of life.

🌍 Expansionism → Fascist Italy pursued territorial expansion and established control over territories including Albania and Ethiopia.

⚔️ Foreign aggression → Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935 and joined Germany and Japan in the Berlin-Tokyo-Rome Axis in 1937.

📌 Significance → Fascist expansion helped weaken international peace and contributed to the outbreak of World War II.

title: 4.5.2 🇩🇪 NAZISM IN GERMANY
notes:
👤 Adolf Hitler → leader of the National Socialist German Workers’ Party, known as the Nazis.

📅 1923 → Hitler attempted to seize power through a coup but failed and was imprisoned.

📖 Mein Kampf → written during his imprisonment and published in 1926.

🎯 Causes of Nazism → German resentment over World War I and the Treaty of Versailles, economic crisis, unemployment, political instability, dissatisfaction with the Weimar Republic and resentment over reparations and territorial losses.

📌 Nazi propaganda also exploited social fears and prejudices to gain popular support.

title: 4.5.3 🇯🇵 MILITARISM IN JAPAN
notes:
🇯🇵 Japanese militarism → developed during the late Meiji period and became especially powerful between 1931 and 1945.

⚔️ Main belief → military leaders should dominate political and social life.

🌏 Expansion → militarists supported territorial expansion and conquest in Asia.

📅 1931 → Japan invaded Manchuria.

📅 1933 → Japan withdrew from the League of Nations after international criticism of its aggression.

📅 1937 → Japan began a wider war against China.

title: 4.6 ⚔️ SECOND WORLD WAR, 1939–1945
notes:
📅 World War II → 1939–1945.

🤝 Allied Powers → mainly Britain, France, the Soviet Union and later the United States.

⚔️ Axis Powers → Germany, Italy and Japan.

🔥 Major causes → aggressive Fascist and Nazi expansion, Japanese militarism, dissatisfaction with the Versailles settlement, the effects of the Great Depression, failure of collective security, appeasement by Britain and France, and weak international opposition to aggression.

📌 Immediate beginning → Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.

title: 4.6.1 🌍 EARLY COURSE OF WWII
notes:
🇵🇱 Poland → Germany used Blitzkrieg tactics and rapidly defeated Polish resistance.

🇫🇷 France → Germany invaded France in May 1940 through Belgium and the Netherlands and defeated the Allied forces.

🇬🇧 Britain → German air attacks attempted to force Britain out of the war, but British resistance prevented invasion.

🇷🇺 Soviet Union → Germany invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941 despite the earlier Nazi-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact.

🇺🇸 United States → Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941, causing the United States to enter the war.

📌 Turning points → Soviet victories at Stalingrad and Kursk helped begin the Allied counter-offensive.

title: 4.6.2 🏆 DEFEAT OF THE AXIS POWERS
notes:
🌍 1943 → Allied forces drove German and Italian forces from North Africa and invaded Italy.

🇫🇷 1944 → France was liberated and Allied forces advanced toward Germany.

🇩🇪 30 April 1945 → Adolf Hitler committed suicide.

🇩🇪 May 1945 → Germany surrendered unconditionally, ending the war in Europe.

🇯🇵 August 1945 → the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

📅 2 September 1945 → Japan surrendered unconditionally and World War II ended.

📌 Why the Axis lost → their forces were spread across huge territories, while the entry of the United States and Soviet Union gave the Allies greater military, economic and manpower resources.

title: 4.6.3 🌎 CONSEQUENCES OF WWII
notes:
💀 Human cost → about 50 million people died, including soldiers and civilians.

🏚️ Destruction → factories, roads, buildings and other infrastructure suffered enormous damage.

🌍 Decolonization → the war accelerated independence movements in Asia and Africa.

🇺🇸🇷🇺 New world powers → the United States and Soviet Union emerged as the two major superpowers.

🧊 Cold War → rivalry between the United States and Soviet Union developed after the war.

🌐 United Nations → the need for a stronger international organization for peace led to the creation of the United Nations, replacing the League of Nations.
